title: Mission Impossible · CartPole 4.0
note: Software coverage and preparation. Real-rig experiments and TA sign-off remain pending. MATLAB sources require execution on a licensed installation.

steps.title: 1 · Model and compare
steps.detail: Nonlinear dynamics, motor/back-EMF, viscous friction, signs and encoders. The 5 V / 10 Hz input is available in Method.
steps.pending: Record the same input on the rig and compare the traces.

steps.title: 2 · Measure friction
steps.detail: Scalar B_f regression plus a Coulomb comparison. Separate estimation and validation segments; weak or poorly excited fits are rejected.
commands: Python CSV: python -m cartpole friction recording.csv
steps.pending: Collect 20–30 seconds of varied motion in both directions. Friction values are still priors until then.

steps.title: 3 · PID balance
steps.detail: Two filtered PID loops, inactive-integrator reset and saturation anti-windup. Position gains follow the course's sign convention.
steps.pending: Lift the pole upright, verify the catch at reduced voltage, then test a small disturbance.

steps.title: 4 · State feedback
steps.detail: A/B/C/D, controllability and observability, pole placement, continuous/discrete LQR and Q/R comparison. LQR is the first-session baseline.
steps.pending: Confirm signs, loop timing and balance before tuning faster poles or larger gains.

steps.title: 5 · Swing-up
steps.detail: Mouse/keys with LQR catch, fixed/phase-locked sine and energy control. All share voltage limits and the track filter.
steps.pending: Identify the rig, validate the fitted model, establish balance, then attempt swing-up. Broad combined uncertainty still causes failures.

steps.title: 6 · Playground
steps.detail: Show reference, PPO, iterative learning, sampling MPC, a 10 cm barrier exercise and Kalman estimation. ILC/MPC are offline experiments.
steps.pending: Hardware exploration follows reliable deterministic control; optional demos are not hardware-qualified.
